nodes.name: Theorem 4.4: classical Lanford-Ruelle
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a shift of finite type and let $f \in \mathrm{SV}(X)$. Every equilibrium measure for $f$ is a Gibbs measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.3: classical Dobrushin
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a strongly irreducible shift space and let $f \in \mathrm{SV}(X)$. Every $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $f$ is an equilibrium measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.9: almost invertible preservation of Gibbsianness
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be an irreducible shift of finite type, let $Y$ be a sofic shift, and let $\pi: X 	o Y$ be an almost invertible factor code. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $X$ which is fully supported, $\sigma$-invariant, ergodic, and $\mathfrak{T}_X$-nonsingular. Let $
u = \pi_* \mu$. Then $
u$ is $\mathfrak{T}_Y$-nonsingular. Moreover, if $\mu$ is Gibbs with respect to an additive cocycle $\phi$, then $
u$ is Gibbs with respect to $\phi \circ (\pi^{-1} 	imes \pi^{-1})$, where $\pi^{-1}$ is well-defined $
u$-almost everywhere.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.9: Dobrushin for irreducible SFTs
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an irreducible shift of finite type and $f\colon X \to \mathbb{R}$  be a potential with summable variation, that is $f \in SV(X)$. Then every $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $f$ is an equilibrium measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.11: almost invertible lifting of Gibbs measures
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be an irreducible shift of finite type, let $Y$ be a sofic shift, and let $\pi: X 	o Y$ be an almost invertible factor code. Let $
u$ be a measure on $Y$ which is fully supported, $\sigma$-invariant, ergodic, and $\mathfrak{T}_Y$-nonsingular. If $
u$ is Gibbs for an additive cocycle $\phi$, then every $\sigma$-invariant measure $\mu$ on $X$ with $\pi_* \mu = 
u$ is  $\mathfrak{T}_X$-nonsingular and, in particular, is a $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $\phi \circ (\pi 	imes \pi)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.11: sofic Dobrushin
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be an irreducible sofic shift and let $f\colon Y \to \mathbb{R}$  be a potential with summable variation, that is, $f \in SV(Y)$. Let $\nu$ be a $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $f$. Then $\nu$ is an equilibrium measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.7: sofic Lanford-Ruelle
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be an irreducible sofic shift and let $f\colon Y \to \mathbb{R}$ be a potential with summable variation, that is, $f \in SV(Y)$. Let $\nu$ be an equilibrium measure for $f$. Then $\nu$ is a Gibbs measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.10: finite-to-one preservation of Gibbsianness
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an irreducible shift of finite type and $Y$ an irreducible sofic shift. Let $\pi: X \to Y$ be a finite-to-one factor code, let $f\colon Y \to \mathbb{R}$  be a potential with summable variation, that is, $f \in SV(Y)$, and let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $f \circ \pi$. Then $\nu = \pi_* \mu$ is a Gibbs measure for $f$.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.12: finite-to-one lifting of Gibbs measures
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an irreducible shift of finite type and $Y$ an irreducible sofic shift. Let $\pi: X \to Y$ be a finite-to-one factor code, let $f\colon Y \to \mathbb{R}$  be a potential with summable variation, that is, $f \in SV(Y)$, and let $\nu$ be a $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure for $f$. Then there exists a $\sigma$-invariant Gibbs measure $\mu$ for $f \circ \pi$ with $\pi_* \mu = \nu$.
